rubric.why: Identifies the taste of monosaccharides and compares it with that of disaccharides.
rubric.description: Monosaccharides are sweet; disaccharides are less sweet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both taste descriptions are correct and linked to the correct carbohydrate groups.
Award 1 mark for stating that polysaccharides are tasteless.

modelAnswer: Monosaccharides have sweet taste. Disaccharides are less sweet in taste. Polysaccharides are tasteless.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both glucose and fructose.
Award 1 mark for naming both sucrose and maltose.

modelAnswer: Two common monosaccharides are glucose and fructose. Two disaccharides are sucrose and maltose.

rubric.why: Identifies starch as a plant storage polysaccharide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that starch is a storage polysaccharide in plants.

modelAnswer: Starch is a storage polysaccharide found in plants.

rubric.why: Identifies the four groups attached to the central carbon in an amino acid.
rubric.description: An amino acid has an amino group, a carboxyl group, hydrogen and a side group (R).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying all four groups.

rubric.why: Shows the groups attached to a central carbon in the amino acid structure.
rubric.description: The groups are attached to a central carbon: H₂N—C(H)(R)—COOH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct structural arrangement with a central carbon attached to H, R, NH₂ and COOH.

modelAnswer: An amino acid is an organic molecule made of an amino group (NH₂), a carboxyl group (COOH), a hydrogen group (H) and a side group (R) which are attached to a central carbon atom. Structure: H₂N—C(H)(R)—COOH.

rubric.why: Identifies all three types of RNA.
rubric.description: The types are messenger RNA (mRNA), transfer RNA (tRNA) and ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all three types.

rubric.why: Describes the functions of mRNA, tRNA and rRNA.
rubric.description: mRNA carries genetic information to ribosomes, tRNA transfers amino acids in the correct sequence, and rRNA forms structural and functional components of ribosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the functions of all three RNA types.

modelAnswer: Messenger RNA (mRNA) carries the genetic information from DNA to the ribosomes during protein synthesis. Transfer RNA (tRNA) transfers specific amino acids to the ribosomes, ensuring the correct sequence during protein synthesis. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) constitutes the structural and functional components of ribosomes, the cellular machinery for protein synthesis.

rubric.why: Explains that DNA's nucleotide sequence contains hereditary information and determines amino acid order during protein synthesis.
rubric.description: DNA contains hereditary information in a nucleotide sequence that determines the order of amino acids during protein synthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the hereditary nucleotide sequence and its role in determining amino acid order.

rubric.why: States that DNA is inherited across generations.
rubric.description: DNA is passed from one generation to the next during reproduction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA passes from one generation to the next during reproduction.

modelAnswer: DNA contains the hereditary information. This information is in the form of a sequence of nucleotides. This sequence determines the order of amino acids during protein synthesis. During reproduction, DNA is passed from one generation to the next.
